title: Early Termination for Hyperdimensional Computing Using Inferential Statistics
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) inference can be terminated early to reduce computation, but existing heuristic early-termination methods lack statistical guarantees and may either unacceptably degrade classification accuracy or terminate inference later than necessary. There is no principled, statistically grounded method for HDC early termination.
motivation: HDC is a promising lightweight paradigm for edge inference on resource-constrained and emerging hardware, making efficiency-accuracy trade-offs via early termination critical; the lack of statistical guarantees in current methods limits their deployability in accuracy-sensitive applications.
method: The method uses statistics—specifically hypothesis testing (a mathematical way to make decisions with measurable confidence)—to decide when to stop classifying. Rather than using an arbitrary cutoff, it checks the similarity scores between the input and each class category (represented as high-dimensional vectors), computes statistical confidence bounds around those scores, and stops inference as soon as it's mathematically confident which category is correct. This provides a provable guarantee on how much accuracy might be lost while reducing unnecessary computation.
key_novelty: This is the first application of formal statistics with provable confidence bounds to determine when to stop inference early in hyperdimensional computing.
contributions: Statistically grounded early-termination framework for HDC classifiers with provable accuracy guarantees.
Formulation of HDC classification confidence as a hypothesis test over hypervector similarity scores.
Demonstration of reduced inference computation vs. heuristic methods while meeting accuracy targets.
limitations: Not discussed; the statistical framework may impose additional online computation overhead that is not quantified.
primary_theme: Statistically guaranteed early termination for HDC
